text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
STANDART
-- The International Monetary Fund (IMF) board is expected to approve today a $659 million reform and funding agreement with Bulgaria, Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov said.

-- Bulgaria's Interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski postponed a visit to Moscow to sign a bilateral gas agreement at the request of the Russia's government, Bulgarian cabinet press centre said. Sofianski was initially expected to leave for Moscow today.
24 CHASA

-- Bulgaria's monthly consumer price inflation fell to 12.3 percent in March from 242.7 in February due to the rise of the national currency, the lev, on the local forex market, the National Statistics Institute said.
-- If the IMF board approves the reform and funding agreement, Bulgaria can receive $175 million as early as next week, Interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski said.
KONTINENT

-- Bulgaria's United Democratic Forces (UDF), favoured to win the April 19 general elections support the reform policies of the caretaker government and will continue them once in power, UDF leader Ivan Kostov said.

-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agancy said it has sold 78 percent of Vinprom wine factory in Rousse for $7.7 million to Dunav-vino, a joint stock company in which the majority stake is held by an Irish firm.
TROUD
-- The Sofia City Court declared the private Trade and Savings Bank insolvent at the request of the Bulgarian National Bank.
-- Bulgaria's United Monarchists, a formation of 15 monarchist parties and organisations, said it would support the main anti-communist United Democratic Forces at the upcoming general elections.
DUMA

-- Bulgaria's Prosecutor General ordered the arrests of three former directors of bankrupt Mineralbank and set bail for three others on suspicion of abusing their positions and illegally extending credits to firms and individuals between 1992 and 1996.
DEMOCRATSIA
-- Bulgaria is expected to lift exports bans on farm products by the July 1 under pledges for trade liberalisation made to international lenders, the cabinet decided.
PARI

-- The European Commission said it has dropped any idea of extending 100,000 tonnes of wheat to Bulgaria as food aid because the country could pay for the grain now that foreign funding has been pledged to it.
-- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
